newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.N. arms envoy holds talks with Iraqi officials.
newsitem.headline: U.N. arms envoy holds talks with Iraqi officials.

text.p: U.N. arms envoy Richard Butler had talks on Thursday with Iraqi officials on Iraq's past biological, chemical and missile weapons programmes, a U.N. official in Baghdad said.

"He is currently meeting (Iraqi presidential adviser) Amir al-Saadi and Iraqi experts on the biological, chemical and missile weapons," Jo Lomas, special assistant to the head of the Ongoing Monitoring and Verification Centre, told Reuters.
She said Butler would have talks with Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz later on Thursday morning, meet him and Iraqi experts again in the evening and brief reporters before leaving Baghdad on Friday.

Butler on July 1 replaced Sweden's Rolf Ekeus, who had led the U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) entrusted with overseeing the dismantling of Iraq's prohibited weapons since its inception soon after the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait.
Butler told reporters on Monday he hoped to be able to close Iraq's weapons file "as soon as possible".

UNSCOM must certify that Iraq has no weapons of mass destruction before the United Nations will lift curbs on Iraqi oil exports, although Baghdad is allowed limited oil exports under a humanitarian deal.
